utterances.text: The document is under the heading of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Mijat Tomic III Battalion, Jablanica, signed by Blaz Azinovic, dated 7th May of '93, with a subject: "Report of the work of the Deputy Commander for SIS, Security and Information Service."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you read the first two paragraphs of that document.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "On 17 April 1993 (Saturday), an armed conflict broke out between HVO/Croatian Defence Council/units and the army of BH in the village of Sovici. On that day, I happened to be at the headquarters in Doljani. "The next day, I was assigned to attend an interrogation of prisoners who had surrendered that day. Mr. Ivan Anderbah conducted the investigation. When the interrogation was over, around 2100 hours on that day, Mr. Ivan took 84 members of the BH army to Ljubuski with him for further handling."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please skip the following paragraph and move down one paragraph to the words -- the sentence which begins "By order from..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "By order from Mr. Vlado Curic (Mr. Tuta's commissioner), the transport of prisoners to Sovicka vrata, together with civilians (women and children), began around 1600 hours on the 5th of May, 1993. From there, in the presence of Mr. Vlado, they were taken to Gornji Vakuf under guard by buses which had been waiting for them there."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of clarification, I heard "Mr. Vlado Juric" in the headphones because I don't have the original text, and that is what I heard from the interpreters. Is that right, is it "Juric"? For the record, please, let us clarify this point, Mr. President, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe Mr. Stringer could ask his question to the witness, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Van Hecke, yes, if you could just state the name again clearly for the record.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: As I did my best to pronounce in the proper way, I thought I said "Curic" and not "Juric." So the "C" with the small -- very well. If you want, I can spell it out for you like it's written in my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again for the record, Mr. President, the original document is a B/C/S document, and so in the translation there's an indication -- some uncertainty about the name, and so I think it's just there in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, could you continue reading the first sentence of the -- first two sentences of the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "After the operation itself, there were instances" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I meant -- did you already read the preceding paragraph on the bottom of --

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- the first page? Could you read that paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "Throughout the operations, the conduct of our army was fair and careful so that we did not have any wounded or dead soldiers. Mr. Tuta commanded the overall operation in this area (Risovac, Sovici and Doljani) in which troops from elsewhere also took part, such as, for instance, the Convicts' Battalion, the Poskok/viper/battalion, the Grdjani, the Posusje mortarmen, and others who I do not know very well."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the next document is Exhibit 389. Can you describe this generally and inform us of the date.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: This is a document under the heading of: "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, HZ H-B, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Office, Jablanica Municipality," dated 13 May 1993, signed by the head of the Defence Office, Marko Rosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just could you read for us the first paragraph, the paragraph which is indicated as Number 1.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "All movable and immovable property of the exiled Muslim population shall be considered war booty and shall belong to the Croatian Defence Council of the HZ H-B."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, finally, I do have one last document to refer to, which is the next one in the binder, Exhibit 418. I may not have one of those for the ELMO. Could you describe this and give us the date, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: This again is a document under the heading of: "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Department," dated in Mostar the 29th of May, 1993, signed by the Commander of the Convicts' Battalion and the Anti-Terrorist Group, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear on this, do you know whether, in fact, the signature appearing on the original language version of this document is, in fact, the signature of Tuta?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, it appears to be similar to other documents I've seen that were signed by the word "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But do you know?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, going back, if you could just read perhaps the heading in the first paragraph of that document.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The heading says: "Order to Commander Stipo Polo. The above-named person is give all authority to control and prevent all criminal activities in the areas of Doljani, Sovici, Risovac and Vrata Cvrsnica and the right to arrest or liquidate them."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, that's all the questions I had concerning this group of documents, and I would propose, then, to move to the next set and would ask that the usher provide the witness with the binder of exhibits which are called "The Seized Documents."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, again, a series of questions about the documents which are in this binder. I believe you testified a little bit already about a search and seizure operation. Have you had an opportunity to review the documents in this binder?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, for the record, the source of these documents, where they were obtained, and when?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: They were obtained during the search and seizure operation we did in the second half of September 1998 in Siroki Brijeg in the location I pointed out on the photo and videos before, known as the tobacco station of Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you describe briefly the manner in which these documents were obtained and how they were kept by the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes. A big scale search operation was set up by the Office of the Prosecutor. As I said before, it was organised by a level higher than myself. So I was more an executioner in this case than the leading agent. So searches took place with search warrants issued by a Judge of the ICTY, the Tribunal, to do searches in three locations; Vitez, Mostar, and Siroki Brijeg. There were three teams of the Office of the Prosecutor went to these three locations. I was, myself, involved in the Siroki Brijeg operation where we went through documents that are kept there in that specific location in Siroki Brijeg in offices of the Ministry of Defence. And documents were seized by us, brought over to The Hague. And again, the same procedure took place as I explained before in bringing these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, the documents in the binder come from where?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: They come from Siroki Brijeg, from the tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me direct you first to Number 589. To give the Trial Chamber an idea of what the documents look like, could you describe this and give us the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Again, as in the previous documents, this is a document under the heading of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Department. It's a certificate. And at the bottom of the page, it has commander of the Convicts' Battalion and ATJ, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, again, just to be crystal clear on this question, I'll ask you to turn the page to the original B/C/S version of this document. I want to focus on the area in which the signature and the title is found and ask you a couple of questions. First of all, is it your testimony or do you know whether the handwritten signature on this document is, in fact, the signature of Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: As I said, at the bottom of the page, you have first mentioning commander of the Convicts' Battalion and ATJ, and then you have a line with the signature, and then the name Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. The signature on the line appears to me to be mentioning Ivan Andabak. So it is certainly not similar to the signature we saw before saying "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then just -- so the record is clear, where the name Naletilic, Tuta appears, it's only the typewritten part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, you are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I apologise for the interruption, but the Defence objects because Mr. Van Hecke is certainly not a handwriting expert. So I don't know how Mr. Van Hecke could identify signatures. So we object on those grounds, that such questions cannot be put to Mr. Van Hecke as he is not an expert witness, an expert in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecution has just asked a question whether it is the signature of your client. It is not asking him to certificate whether it is or not, just out of his knowledge whether he can see if it is the signature of your client or not. I'm not quite sure that your objection [sic] is valid. Maybe Mr. Stringer could guide us in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I can't disagree strongly with what counsel has said because, clearly, the witness is not in a position to identify signatures. I can tell the Trial Chamber what I am trying to do, because I think that unless there's some clarification right at the beginning on this point, one could look at the English translation, and one could just draw the conclusion that, in fact, the original document unquestionably bears the signature of the accused Naletilic. And to the extent that someone might be misled by that, I simply wanted to raise the issue at the very start that the translation may indicate something which is not precisely the case. So in other words, I don't want to be raising the view or suggesting that in our view, all of these were, in fact, personally signed by the accused. Because there may be, in fact, a question on that which does not appear on the face of the English language translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you must hear the explanations from Mr. Stringer on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, I heard them, and I also consulted with my colleagues, but I won't detain you any longer. I'll try to clear all these matters up in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit that I would direct your attention to is Exhibit Number 613. And then could you just describe this document and tell us the date, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Again, this is a similar document to the previous one. So again the heading of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Department, dated 29 September, 1993, saying "Certificate" as title. And again at the bottom, commander of the Convicts' Battalion and ATG, signature of Ivan Andabak, mentions here Mladen Naletilic, Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next exhibit is Exhibit 704. I'll ask that the first page of the exhibit be placed on the ELMO. Can you describe this document for us, please. Give us the date.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The date is 2nd of December, 1993. The heading says Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Department, Convicts' Battalion, and ATJ. Subject: Salary lists for November 1993. At the bottom, the words, "Commander of the Convicts' Battalion and Anti-Terrorist Unit, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then the next page of the translation, again, if you could indicate, there is a group at the top and a group at the bottom, and I want to focus on the group at the bottom. If you could just focus on that group called Specification of the Convicts' Battalion and ATJ, or ATG. Do you see on this document an indication or a reference to the ATG Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you point to that, please, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again, moving farther down again, who is indicated as the commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, for the sake of the record, you have to describe that, your witness is pointing which name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, maybe you could just give us an indication of where that is found on page 2 of this English translation.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: When we look at page 2 of this English translation, the document, before we come to the name under the page on the third last line, we see the words "Vinko Skrobo, ATJ" and the figure "85" behind it. And at the very bottom of the page, the last two lines, I would say, says on the second-last line, "Commander," and on the last one, "Mladen Naletilic, Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to direct your attention to page 10 of the English translation of Exhibit 704. And directing your attention to the first name that appears on that page, what is that name?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: First name, also with the number "1" in front of it, says Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this is a name that appears on one of the earlier documents which we just reviewed, I believe, Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, it appears to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know the present whereabouts of Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: For the moment, Ivan Andabak is in custody in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why is he in custody there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: He is alleged to be involved in the transport of 600 kilos of cocaine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is he the subject of any other criminal proceedings of which you are aware?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Mr. Andabak is also indicted in Bosnia-Herzegovina for the moment on alleged giving the orders to assassinate the Deputy Minister of the Interior of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if I could direct you to page 30 of the English translation of this document. I asked you previously if you had seen the name of the Vinko Skrobo, ATG. Do you see it on this page; and can you tell us, if so, where it's located.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, on this page under the heading saying Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Defence Department, Convicts' Battalion and ATJ, with the reference number, and Siroki Brijeg, 2nd of December, 1993. After this heading, on the first line, we see Vinko Skrobo, ATJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The first name which appears on that page, can you tell us the name and also the title.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It's marked with a number 1 just after Vinko Skrobo, ATJ. We see Vinko Martinovic with the title "Commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. This appears to be a list of names which continues on to the next page. So I'll ask you to turn the next page. And at the bottom of the page, if you could tell us again what name appears there.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, we have the same two last lines like in the other document, saying at the second last, "Commander," and at the last, "Mladen Naletilic, Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how many names appear on this list of Vinko Skrobo, ATJ?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: 85 names appear on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Referring back to page 2 of the English translation, does that number 85 appear to correspond to anything that's found on this page 2?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, on the line I marked before on this page 2, the third last line, saying Vinko Skrobo, ATJ, has at the end of that line the number 85.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next exhibit is 753. Could you describe this document, please, and tell us the date.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: This is a document under the heading Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Defence, Convicts' Battalion, with the reference number and Siroki Brijeg, 8th of March, 1994, titled "Certificate." And at the bottom, I see the word "Commander," and under there, "Mladen Naletilic, Tuta," signed and stamped.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in the body of this document, beginning with the middle with the word "wounded in the right arm..." could you just read those three lines, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "Wounded in the right arm by an enemy shell in Rastani action on 22nd of September, 1993. Wounded in the head (on the right cheek) by a bullet and in the right leg during combat on the Bulevar while defending Mostar on 11th December, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As you have said, this refers to someone named Robert Kolobaric. What I would like to ask you to do now is go back to Exhibit Number 704. Directing your attention to page 9 of the English translation, do you find the name of Robert Kolobaric on this list from the Combat Group 6?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What number is that on page 9?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: He is under the number 3 on page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. 757. Can you describe that for us, please, and give us the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Document is, again, under the heading Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Defence, Convicts' Battalion, with the registration number, Siroki Brijeg, 8th of March, 1994. Titled "Certificate." At the bottom, it says, "Commander, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could just -- if this document indicates the date of the founding of the Convicts' Battalion, could you please read. I'm referring specifically to the third line.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It starts with the name of a person from Siroki Brijeg was a member of the Convicts' Battalion of the HVO, Croatian Defence Council, from the date it was founded the 1st of June, 1991, until the 27th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is Exhibit 804. Can you give a general description of this document and the date, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The document is under the heading of: "The Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Defence, Mostar Defence Administration, Siroki Brijeg Defence Office," dated "Siroki Brijeg, 20 February 1996," with a "Decision" titled, signed by Head of Office Marinko Mikulic, and a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Directing your attention to page 2, the English translation, there are a series of bulleted points in the body of the document there, and I'd like to direct you to the fourth bulleted point which begins "As a member of..." Could you please read that one.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "As a member of the Convicts' Battalion of Siroki Brijeg, he injured his left knee," then with a question mark "(a ligament/a ligament inside the left knee joint was severe) in Doljani near Jablanica on the 19th of April, 1993, while carrying out orders in the course of his military duties."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the last document from this group, Mr. President, would be Exhibit 809. And just a description and a date, please.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, again, it has the same heading as the previous document, dated "Siroki Brijeg, 2nd of May, 1996." And at the end of the document, it says, "Head: Marinko Mikulic" and a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And turning your attention to page 2 of the translation, the sixth bulleted point, about a third of the way down the page, beginning with the words, "That the above-named..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "That the above-named, while a member of the Convicts' Battalion VP/Military Post Code/1717, on the 16th of May, 1993, in the Bulevar, Mostar municipality, during the execution of a combat operation, was wounded by a shell fragment in the right shin and in the neck, and that the wounding occurred in the execution of an order."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, that is all of the seized documents that we wanted to discuss. And now, Mr. President, I can ask that the witness be shown the last group, which is in a binder of documents labelled "Croatian Government." This is one of the blue plastic binders, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, have you had an opportunity to examine the documents that are collected in this binder previously?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the source of these documents?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The source of these document is the government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us when these documents were obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, not the exact date. Again, they were obtained in the course of investigation and were requested by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you say "were requested by the Office of the Prosecutor," can you give a little more -- give us more information about how the Prosecutor requested documents from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, again - excuse me - a request was made by the Office of the Prosecutor through the embassy of Croatia, Republic of Croatia, here in The Hague, who then in turn sent the request further to Zagreb, after which the documents came back in the reverse order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in order to determine the precise dates on which these documents were provided to the Prosecutor's office, well, are you -- do you know, as we speak now, the exact date involved?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact date from the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. How would you go about finding that out?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, I can go through the databases of the Office of the Prosecutor and could find the date when they were received, because it's all marked, of course, on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Nonetheless, though, it's your testimony that these were specifically provided in response to a request for assistance or a request?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know how they would have been maintained, then, by the Prosecutor's office after they were obtained from the government of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, again they would have been -- you see, again if you go through the binder, the unique number that is on each page, so they were brought into evidence again through the same system I explained before in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are five documents in this set which we would propose to examine, the first of which is Exhibit Number 688.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Van Hecke, let me first ask you to read the very -- well, I'm sorry, let me back up. If you could just give us a description and the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The heading on top of the document says: "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council." It's subtitled: "Military Police Administration, Military Police Criminal Department, Mostar Centre." It's dated, "Mostar, 25th of November, 1993". At the bottom of the document, it says: "Head of the centre, Officer Toni Ramljak."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, directing your attention back to the first page, there's a title or a subject of the document, and then if you could read the subject and also the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The "Subject" says: "Report on an incident involving members of the Convicts' Battalion." The first paragraph reads: "At 1535 hours on 24 November 1993, in the Palace Cafe in Ljubuski, Jakov Beljo, also known as Splico, member of the HVO/Croatian Defence Council/Convicts' Battalion from Siroki Brijeg, was seriously wounded by a gunshot fired from a nine-millimetre CZ M-75 pistol, factory number B9436. The shot was fired by Robert Nosic, who left the scene after the event."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you would please turn the page to page 2 of the English translation, and if you could read for us, please, the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "Around 2320 hours, an operations duty officer of the 5th MP" - Military Police - "HVO Battalion came to the premises of the department and reported that 50 to 60 members of the Convicts' Battalion had disarmed the Ljubuski MP Administration and that they were coming to Mostar, to collect the accused."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then skipping down to the next -- the second paragraph, which begins with the words, "Thirty to 35..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "Thirty to 35 persons armed with long and short weapons and hand grenades raided the premises of the MP Criminal Department and the MP Intervention Group officers' dormitory. They ordered all the members of the Military Police they found - about seven or eight of them were there at the time - to lie down and proceeded to disarm them."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then if you could again skip the next paragraph and go to the second one, which begins, "The armed members..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "The armed members of the Convicts' Battalion were personally commanded by Mr. Mladen Naletilic, also known as Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again if you could skip the next paragraph and move down to the paragraph beginning, "After spending..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "After spending 15 minutes on the first floor, all members of the Convicts' Battalion left the premises of the Department, taking the accused Nosic along with them. Nosic had until that moment been guarded by the officers of the MP Intervention Group on the premises of the MP Criminal Department."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, finally, if you could read the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "Officers of the MP Criminal Department warned Mr. Mladen Naletilic that this was not the way to ensure the legality of the proceedings, and that what he was doing would achieve nothing. Mr. Naletilic turned a deaf ear and blamed Mr. Biskic in person for everything that happened."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next document I would refer you to is Number 687, which is a previous -- it's an earlier document in the binder. If you could give a description of this document and the date.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It's a document under - excuse me - the general heading of: "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Department of Defence, Convicts' Battalion, 1st ATJ/anti-sabotage unit. Siroki Brijeg, November 25, 1993." It says, "Report," and at the bottom of the document, it says: "Commander of the Convicts' Battalion 1st ATJ, Mladen Naletilic, also known as Tuta," with a signature on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just directing you to the B/C/S document which is behind that, the second page of that. Can you just tell us, the name which is handwritten in there, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: The name handwritten, and just above the name is "Tuta" or appears to be "Tuta."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, going back to the English translation and turning to the second page, going down to the fifth line, which begins, "The Military Police..." If you could just start reading there and read the rest of the text.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "The Military Police did not manage to arrest two executioners: the late Robert Nosic from Radisici, while Mirko Bunoza, also known as Hakalo, accomplice to this ruthless murder is at large, and a group from the Convicts' Battalion is looking for him. "In these war circumstances, it does not matter to us whether the reason for the Military Police not doing its job is fear or animosity towards the Convicts' Battalion, as the fact remains that the Military Police has not done its job in a single case. The Commander of the Convicts' Battalion has given the order for Mirko Bunoza, also known as Hakalo, to be punished, believing this to be the only way to protect the soldiers of the Convicts' Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then down to Exhibit Number 696, please. Could you describe this document for us, please, and give us the date.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It's a document under the heading: "Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, HVO/Croatian Defence Council/Main Staff, SIS/Security and Information Service/ And Military Police Sector," dated, "Posusje, 26 November 1993," addressed to HVO Convicts' Battalion Commander Mladen Naletilic personally, and at the bottom of the document the words: "Chief, Colonel Marjan Biskic."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now on page 1 of the English translation, the last paragraph beginning with the words "The Convicts' Battalion..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "The Convicts' Battalion, which was under your command, did not act in accordance to the law and the HVO regulation book because they took justice into their own hands. They forcefully entered the MP Administration premises and disarmed all the officials. Then they forcefully entered into the premises of the MP 5th Battalion in Mostar, disarmed the members of the MP and, using force, took away the perpetrator of the crime, Robert Nosic, and a MP Administration Officer, Mr. Zeljko Dzidic."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is Exhibit 707. Before it goes on the ELMO, Mr. President, before I forget, this is a document which we would at least provisionally tender under seal. It contains information about other areas, other events which are unrelated to this case, and it also involves -- or actually I should say it contains the names of victims of sexual assaults, and for that reason it's not necessary really for this case and we think that it's appropriate to tender the document under seal at least provisionally until we can redact names of rape victims from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, are we going to the private session when we're discussing this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The issue won't be raised during the examination, nor will those parts of the document be put on the ELMO. But I just wanted to note it now before -- frankly, before I forget.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, could you please describe generally what Exhibit 707 is.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, it's a very large document saying: "Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Defence, Security and Information Service, Administration," "Mostar, 4 December, 1993," directed to Croatian Information Service, to Mr. M. Tudjman personally, and saying: "Enclosed with this document is part of the findings on crimes in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, turning to page 43 of the English translation - and we can put that on the ELMO - the bottom of the page, the section begins, "Regarding the Convicts' Battalion..." Could you just please read the first three lines of that section.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: So the heading says: "The Convicts' Battalion." Then it says: "As you requested, we are sending you a report on our findings on the illegal activities of the members of the Convicts' Battalion. But, we would like to point out that these are only cases /from/ sources we have found to be reliable."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then turning to page 45 of the English translation, I'd like to direct your attention to the second full paragraph and ask you to read that.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "At about 2200 hours on 21 September 1993 a group of soldiers went to Biljana Miljus's flat on Splitska Street 66/4 and took her away. The soldiers were looking for some man, but when they saw Biljana they started beating her and took her away by force in an unknown direction. These soldiers have been identified as members of the Vinko Skrobo Anti-Terrorist Group from the Convicts' Battalion from Siroki Brijeg."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then moving to the very bottom of that same page, the last paragraph which begins with, "On 29 September..."

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "On 29 September 1993 in the evening, men from the Vinko Skrobo Anti-Terrorist Group and the 1st Light Assault Battalion arrested a large group of Muslim civilians in the Centre 2 neighbourhood. The men were then imprisoned in the SVIZ Heliodrom, and the women and the children were taken over to the left, Muslim side of the Neretva."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the final document is Exhibit Number 830.1. Mr. Van Hecke, yes, if you could describe this document for us, please. Tell us its date.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: This document is under the heading: "Republic of Croatia, County Court in Zagreb, Zrinjevac Number 5," so Case Number VII K-216/97, "Record of 17 December 1997 of the continued main hearing before the County Court in the city of Zagreb."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Van Hecke, did you attend the court hearing that's referred to in this record?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I was present in the courtroom, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I went there to monitor that day in the trial of Mr. Naletilic, who was a defendant in this case, on the day that also Mr. Vinko Martinovic would appear as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you know, from having gone to Zagreb, what were the charges against Mr. Naletilic in the Zagreb proceeding of this day?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: There were several charges, including kidnapping of a person filed against police on duty and a sentence of murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do any of those charges relate to some of the earlier seized documents that we have just finished looking at?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes. The first two charges relate to the previous documents where we talked about Mr. Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, directing your attention to a page -- what is indicated as page 89 of this English translation, beginning at the top where it says, "Vinko Martinovic is called into the courtroom..." Can you begin reading there and read down the next four paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: "Vinko Martinovic is called into the courtroom. Witness Vinko Martinovic, son of Ivan, born 21st of September, 1963 in Mostar, from Mostar, Splitska Street, Number 1, caterer, unrelated to the accused. "The witness is advised to the effect of Article 219, Article 221, and Article 315, paragraph 1, of the Law on Criminal Procedure. "I have lived in Mostar all my life and was there also when the war broke out, and I stayed in Mostar throughout the war. During the war, I joined in actively on the Croatian side of becoming an HVO member. As an HVO member for the duration of the war, I was a member of the 4th HOS Battalion, and then an 11 [as printed] member of the Convicts' Battalion, which Convicts' Battalion changed its name later five times in terms of formation. It is established that the witness corrects his statement and says that it was not the name Convicts' Battalion that was changed, but that brigades changed within Herceg-Bosna formation-wise. "The commander of the Convicts' Battalion itself was the accused Mladen Naletilic. And to my knowledge, the headquarters of his command was at Siroki Brijeg at the Tobacco Station. In addition to this location, the Convicts' Battalion was divided into four smaller units, and further into yet smaller ones, the way it is in military structure. And each one had its command HQ in different places. I was with the part of the Convicts' Battalion which was in charge of Mostar, so that our seat was in Mostar, in Zagrebacka Street, in the building today used by the Ministry of Defence. Within that part of the Convicts' Battalion, I was commander of the unit called Vinko Skrobo. I do not know who was superior to the commander of the Convicts' Battalion, i.e., who his commander was. That, namely, is a difficult question. This was the military authorities set up in the part which I know about."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Van Hecke, were you present in the courtroom in Zagreb when this testimony took place?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness. May I -- I apologise. I forgot, as I often do, to tender the exhibits. There are a lot of them. What I have done is to make a list of all of the exhibit numbers for the various exhibits, photographs, videotapes, documents. And if it would assist the Trial Chamber and the Registrar, I could circulate this list as a way to identify all of the documents we are tendering at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I failed to bring a sufficient number of copies of this. I could easily produce additional sets of this list, perhaps during the break or whenever. It is simply a matter of running back to my computer and printing it off a couple more times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think at least the Defence lawyers are entitled to have copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Or we can make copies now and distribute additional copies in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Why don't we deal with this in our proceedings tomorrow morning when everybody is probably informed at least of the documents. Shall we begin the cross-examination first?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think that that would be a wise use of the time that remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination. Mr. Krsnik, are you going to do some cross-examination to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, of course. But not to take too much of your time, I'll try to do my best, because you can see the quantity of documents that we have here, and you have heard all our objections. And I repeat, we've only just now learned about the testimony of this witness. We barely heard what was the substance of his testimony during these two days. So that I shall try to do -- to cross-examine this witness as best I know and can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. I have no doubt about your ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Van Hecke. I am Mr. Kresimir Krsnik, chief counsel for the accused Mladen Naletilic. Since you were at Zagreb in Siroki Brijeg, I believe we have already met. I shall begin with a cross-examination what is freshest in our mind, that is the documents. So I might start backwards. So the first question that I would like to ask you would be, Do you speak Croatian?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I don't. I know a few words only. So that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you followed the trial in Zagreb, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you understand the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I had next to me an interpreter in the courtroom, whispering in my ear what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the judicial procedure in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I certainly don't know with anything -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If you were in the courtroom, did you notice any witness for -- takes the notes like it is done here and referring to notes as it is done here?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you aware of the rights of the accused before Croatia courts?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Not completely, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you do know something, do you? Did you study Croatian criminal law?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, from the Court records, it transpires, as we can see -- will you please look at it. You have it? Good. It transpires that there was a comment of the accused, a comment of sorts of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Can you lead me to the exact place, please. It's pretty long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The Croatian translation, page 6.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I think I found it back in the English translation. I assume that you refer to the -- in the English translation, page 91, to the sentence in the middle of the page: "It is established that at the moment the accused interrupts of his own initiative, remarking, I ordered that he should be taken to that place."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you know what I was going to ask you?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It was a remark of the...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no. My only question was that it transpired from the record that a comment was included there. I did not say whose or who it referred to. May I ask my question? How is the record kept in Croatian court? The court record before the Croatian court, is it the same technique as here before this Chamber in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you know how the record is kept? Did you see it being kept in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I know somebody was writing down what was happening, but I don't know exactly how they do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you didn't notice that first everybody would say whatever he had to say, and that only after that, the judge would dictate the summary; or that is, the presiding judge would dictate it for the record?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So all that is said in the courtroom is not included in the record, because it is the presiding judge dictates in for the record what he deems necessary?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is all that was said in this courtroom reflected in this record?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, it's, of course, difficult to remember everything that was said in court, because the proceedings take some time. I think what is written down here is a reflection of what happened in the courtroom that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know how that trial ended?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, to my knowledge, there was no acquittal nor a sentencing in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where did you get that information from?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I don't know. I got so much information. I can't recall where I got the information from. I assume, and I only assume, and it's dangerous, of course, that it also came from the Croatian government. But I can't state this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it an oral information or was it in writing, what you received from the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In Croatia, can the executive branch of power interfere in the judicial branch of power?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know who is responsible for information about court proceedings in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I'm afraid I missed one word. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Regarding the information about different proceedings before Croatian courts, who is in charge of providing information about those proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I don't [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is the Croatian government responsible for producing such information?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was Mr. Naletilic arrested lawfully in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: That's, I assume, something that the Republic of Croatia has to find out for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you are an investigator who conducts very exhaustive investigations. I'm asking you if, during your exhaustive investigation, you found that whether the treatment of my client was in accordance with law.

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, as I explained before, heading an investigation team, or one of us heading an investigation team with different branches. So part of my investigation team are legal advisors or legal advisors or lawyers who work in very close cooperation with me. So I am to assume that they looked into the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know where the alleged crimes were committed and where the trial took place, the trial for those alleged crimes took place?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I know the alleged crimes took place in Hercegovina, so within Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the trial took place inside the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you did not find it odd?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Can I explain why I don't find it odd? No, I didn't find it odd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No. Do you know when cases can be conducted for crimes committed in either territory of the different state under Croatian law?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I don't know it under Croatian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you followed that trial as a member of the investigating team?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me: Were you present at the hearing when the bail was offered for his release?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you know what followed after the Court's decision to accept it and that the accused could be released?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did the Office of the Prosecutor of which you make the part as investigator take any steps on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I don't know if steps were made at that occasion or others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you aware that detention was requested by this Tribunal -- or rather, by the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: As I say, the legal matters are mainly dealt with by the legal advisors of the team. I, as a team leader, have mainly organisational and administrative power.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This case was provoked -- or rather, it was conducted following an order to arrest my client so that he could be turned over to this Tribunal. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: I can tell you because from the top of my head, your client was arrested in the course of February 1997, and we started our investigation and decided to start the investigation in March of 1997, after his arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then how is it that there are statements of some witnesses which date back to '95?

utterances.speaker: JAN VAN HECKE
utterances.text: Well, there is a very simple explanation for it. In the course of other investigations, the name of your client came up by witnesses who were interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see it is 4.00, and I am going to move on to a different topic. Tomorrow I will try to see to make my cross-examination as efficient and as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding us of the time. We'll adjourn to tomorrow morning, 9.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of September, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.00 p.m.,
